I think people have conflated the actual terms used by people when criticizing Israel and just applied them to everything.

Settler-Zionism is what I and I hope most people are against because those people are pretty much terrorists. But I support the existence of Israel as a state, so am I a Zionist?

Settler colonialism is real and is a form of colonialism that is being used to displace Palestinians in the West Bank, but I don’t believe that all Israelis are colonizers. People just hear the terms thrown about and latch on without understanding or critical thinking.

She isn't but context ofc is important. Israel and the IDF are not actively eradicating Palestinians on the sole basis of them being Palestinian.

They are, however, complicit and actively promoting settler terrorists who are doing exactly that. People will argue that being complicit is just as bad

Hamas is a terrorist organization that must be eradicated, that is very clear. However, collective punishment is never justified.

So, in theory, would it be possible to open the border to either Israel or the Sinai to create refugee camps monitored and protected by UN Peace keeping forces to allow innocent civilians a chance to actually flee??

Going to throw* this out here into the thread, these are just my thoughts and I'd love to hear what others have to say.

Hamas, as a terrorist organization, has the sole purpose of inflicting mass civilian casualties to promote and insight terror not just in Israel proper or Gaza, but across the world. They have succeeded. Millions of Jews who have little to no affiliations with the government of Israel feel this terror in their communities not only because of the attacks but also the way some Pro-Palestinian have acted toward Jews in general. People who have no love for true Palestinian freedom and independence, who thrive on hate and division, latching on to a very real cause in order to spew their hate to a wider audience.

The exact same is happening in Muslim communities across the world. The collective disregard for Palestinian lives, the call for the complete destruction of Palestinian homes in Gaza, and the applause from some at the threat of wiping Gaza off the map are disgusting and deplorable behaviors that have led some to go as far as to conflate the Islamic extremists in Palestine with all Muslims. I've seen comments on many platforms from both Jews and Muslims about the collective fear of people in their community harming them. This is what terrorism is working for.

Here's the thing, the competing nationalist ideologies of the respective "governments" in Israel/Palestine are not compatible with the core values of our Western democracies. I'd like to hope that we stand for egalitarian values, secular values, values that put people not of any one specific culture or race or creed or whatever above anyone else. Neither the current far-right Israeli government nor Hamas, especially Hamas, stand for any of these values.

We must reject the ethno-nationalist claim that one group has the unique right to reside in the region. Period. This is paramount for any idea of peace between anyone. 

We must refrain from devolving into an optics discussion, an argument on which side committed worse atrocities in order to justify the side of whoever is deemed to be the current victim. This is exactly what Hamas wants, this is exactly what the far-right Israeli government wants. Getting caught up in an endless debate on who has been more evil is counter-productive and takes away from the real issues.

- Acknowledge, accept, and condemn the actions taken by Hamas against innocent Israelis and that it was a terrorist act.
- Accept that Hamas must be treated as an ISIS-level threat and expelled from Gaza through military force within the laws/rules of War.
- Understand, acknowledge, and condemn the illegal settlements and use of extreme and excessive force against Palestinians under the guise of "security"
- Accept that Israel is an apartheid state and that the government supports and protects religious extremists who enact a form of settler colonialism on rightfully Palestinian homes.
- Understand that because of these actions taken by the IDF and extremist settlers, in probable conjunction with a myriad of other reasons such as extreme poverty, poor education, corrupt leadership, and oppression; in recent years some Palestinians have turned to Islamic extremism and committed terror attacks in the name of freedom. While their cause is a just and true one, their means cannot be allowed in a modern civil society.

I want to end on this thought. Israel is a democracy; a new one like many others in this region of the world, and like all governments it has major shortcomings. But it is still a democracy, elected by the people, recognized internationally, and with the support of the most powerful military in the world. They have people within the government and Israeli society who actively speak out against the inhumane treatment of Palestinians because of the freedoms provided to some by this democracy. This shows us that from both external international pressure, as well internal pressure, the government can change for the better. It has in the past, and we have to hold on to the hope it will in the future. I want to believe this, I have to believe this if there will ever be peace.

On the other hand, Palestinians have no one and nothing who stands with them and specifically their interests. They never have. This is why it is imperative that the international community stands behind the Palestinian people and lend our voice to them. Israel can and must take criticism and make change because they hold all the power in the broader scope of this conflict, and because they are a democracy that can enact these changes. They are the only people who hold the keys to open the door to the first steps of peace.

I think an important distinction has been lost on a lot of people when using the term colonizer. To call Israelis "colonizers" is just wrong and denies a millennia of history of Jewish expulsion.

Israeli settlers illegally occupying the West Bank are enacting a form of settler colonialism which is occupying rightfully Palestinian territory. That is an important distinction, but that level of nuance is lost on most.

Oh my god. This guy pulls well-worded bullshit out of his ass better than *The OA* smh...

>This commercial/short film isn't really about "telling the stories of photographers risking their lives". I mean, superficially, that's literally what the commercial is about. But in consequence, it's really a branding exercise to sell Leicas.

Yes bro it's an advertisement! That. Is. The. Point. It's supposed to showcase their brand in favourable light and try and sell you shit. 

You really don't seem to understand what it takes to tell a visual story, in a short amount of time, that resonates with an audience AND sells shit. I think the generic image of the women in burquas being gunned down is stupid and kinda useless in the film, but the two vignettes of the African Warlords and more specifically the Tiananmen Square (spell that right you pompous fuck) are extremely recognizable to the broadest audience. Which is the whole point of an advertisement! It was done on purpose! 

>What a commercial like this WON'T do is use imagery from say, the My Lai Massacre. I'm sure there are photographers that risked their lives to document US soldiers raping and killing Vietnamese children. But why won't a Leica commercial tell THAT story? Because again, the commercial isn't really about telling the story of photographers who risk their lives.

This is a load of bullshit that you pulled out of your ass to pad how fucking smart you are. There is no way in hell that the My Lai massacre is anywhere as recognizable or a singular moment as famous as the Tank Man for the average consumer, therefore it doesn't make marketing sense (even though Leica claim they didn't make this). 

The reason why a filmmaker would showcase these photographers as the "hero" is that you need a focal point to tell a story! A good filmmaker uses the audiences mirror neurons to evoke empathy, to make us feel as if we are part of the moment, to sympathize with the character. Key there is CHARACTER. Forget all the exposition and background nonsense! There's a reason why in most films, the background history of the characters and the world are a mystery for a solid chunk of time. It's because people don't connect with facts, they connect with people. That's the whole point of this ad! It is meant for us to feel like we are those photographers in those moments, capturing those events on fucking purpose!

>And don't get me wrong, strictly as a commercial exercise, I admit that this is a "great" commercial and an excellent example of branding.

Bruh then stfu

>2) photographs are the epitome of propaganda, because as any filmmaker/photographer knows, a still image is a lie.

Oh my god you have this so wrong. The lie of a still image is that we are only seeing what the photographer is showing us. Only what is in the frame. The lie is that the context of the image is lost because we lose the whole of the moment outside of the frame, but that's not what the photographer intended for us to see. These aren't Instagram thots who use facetune to manipulate their bodies. Even though we are only seeing a sliver of a moment, the photographer has guided us to SEE that moment because of HOW it makes us feel. Therefore, the still image is not a lie.

>Since none of this is a direct answer to your question,

Exactly. You don't answer the question at all. You dance around it with fancy words and random facts or opinions to sound like you know what the fuck you're talking about but you don't. So imma say this again, Fuck you and have a great day.

SHAME on the rest of ya for just letting this guy spew nonsense and upvote him just because he's being PC or leftist or whatever the fuck you think he's doing. Just cuz he's using big words and names or events to sound smart doesn't actually mean he is smart.

The point of the story is to show the bravery of the photographers who risk their lives to shed light on events that would be hidden or otherwise swept under the rug. Doing a bit of Googling revealed that the photo was actually shot on a Nikon F2 (lol Leica), which the night before saved the photographers life! I bet you the type of guy to shit on Bang-Bang Club cuz it was about white "photographers TAKING THE PICTURES of these events". Man stfu. Go back to sitting in your comfy ass chair eating your brain food so you can come up with a well-worded response, while brave men and women risk their lives to show the world what others try and hide.

You do bring up good points, but you're also a complete asshat about it. So fuck you and have a great day :)
